newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Slow week ends slowly.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Slow week ends slowly.

text.p: Asian debt markets ended a slow week slowly with just a couple of new issues.
Amsteel Capital Holdings launched a US$50 million floating rate note via Peregrine Capital and Overseas Union Bank.
The three-year FRN was priced at par to float at 135 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
With fees, the all-in return for top-tier managers is 140 basis points.
Malaysian companies are not big issuers in the international capital markets, but Amsteel and companies related to Amsteel have been in the market a few times.
Indonesia's Bank Bira brought a US$80 million FRN. Merrill Lynch is the bookrunner.
The two-year paper pays a coupon of 90 basis points over LIBOR and an all-in return of 135 basis points.
Union Bank of Bangkok closed its US$20 million FRN, and a few details emerged on Commercial Bank of Korea's upcoming US$100 million deal.
A few of the issues that were expected this week now look set to launch next week, including issues for Korean borrowers Korea Merchant Banking Corp and Pusan Leasing.
The long-awaited Yankee bond for the Philippines National Power Corp could launch in the next couple of weeks, bankers said.
